tools.name: delegate
tools.description: Start an opencode worker (a cheaper model run by the opencode CLI) on a self-contained task, in the background. Use it for simple exploration or for code changes that follow a plan already written down: the worker has none of this conversation, so the prompt must hold every file path, decision and acceptance check it needs. Returns at once with a worker id; the person watches progress and diffs in the opencode pane. Collect the result with the status tool (pass wait_seconds to block until it ends), then verify the work yourself (read the files, run the tests) — a worker report is a claim, not proof. Workers running in the same folder must not touch the same files. To correct or extend a finished worker, use follow_up rather than starting over. Deny rules stop a worker from committing, pushing or switching branches, deleting files, installing packages, reading or editing .env files, reaching outside its folder and running any command the user denied for their stack: leave those steps out of the brief and do them yourself. The rules match command patterns and are no sandbox, so review what a worker changed.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Report on opencode workers. With id: that worker in full (files changed, recent activity, final answer). Without id: one line per worker. wait_seconds (≤600) blocks until the worker (or, without id, every running worker) ends or the time runs out.

tools.name: follow_up
tools.description: Send another instruction to a finished opencode worker, in the same opencode session (it keeps its context). The worker runs again in the background; collect it with status.

tools.name: stop
tools.description: Stop a running opencode worker by id.

children: Ask Claude to delegate a well-scoped task to opencode.
